thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 Pager: p99 tail latency breach for customer Silvercrest on dedicated-pool-4 (region: us-west-2). Current symptom: streaming responses stalling, large time gaps between chunks. Escalation level: page.\n
alice_oncall: I'm on it. @ben_reliability @carla_sre please join — this looks like a single-tenant tail problem. Any early hypotheses?\n
ben_reliability: first glance from metrics — sudden jump in p95/p99 for stream chunk latency at 08:12 UTC, coincides with a spike in concurrent sessions from Silvercrest. Their session count went from ~80 to ~420 over 30s.\n
carla_sre: logs show repeated KV cache eviction loops on the worker nodes for pool dedicated-pool-4-*. Eviction rate spiked at same time. Might be thrash.\n
dave_engine: adding more: worker pods are showing high memory churn and repeated GC pauses in the python runtime that runs the preproc and stream aggregator. Stack traces attached below.\n
emma_support: Luis from Silvercrest on the line, he reports user-facing stalls and retries. He says they rolled out a heavy batch of parallel prompt generation for a customer demo. Luis, can you confirm request patterns (prompt sizes, concurrency, streaming vs non-streaming)?\n
luis_silvercrest: yes, we started a demo at 08:10 UTC. Each client opened 6 parallel streams, typical prompt length 3–4k tokens, and many sessions used long prefixes. We didn't expect so many simultaneous sessions. Sorry for the blast.\n
alice_oncall: ok. Short-term mitigation options: 1) throttle Silvercrest concurrency at the ingress for their org id, 2) route them to a fallback model variant with lower memory/KV usage, 3) temporary cluster scale-up. Which is fastest?\n
ben_reliability: fastest is org-level throttle via org-proxy (config flip). Routing to fallback also quick if we have a compatible quantized variant in us-west-2; check model catalog. Scale-up will take several mins + GPU cold spin.\n
carla_sre: I can apply a conservative throttle: set max_concurrent_sessions=150 for org=silvercrest. Command: ```./opsctl set-org-quota --org silvercrest --max-concurrency 150 --ttl 30m```\n
alice_oncall: do it. Also enable verbose tracing for one worker to capture pprof and KV cache metrics. Carla, can you get a pprof snapshot?\n
carla_sre: running pprof dump on pod dedicated-pool-4-1a2b: ```kubectl exec -it pod/dedicated-pool-4-1a2b -- curl http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=20 > /tmp/silvercrest.pprof``` uploading to shared bucket now.\n
carla_sre: throttle applied. org proxy logs show 429s introduced at 08:18 UTC for new sessions beyond throttle. We'll watch.\n
ben_reliability: routed a small fraction of traffic to fallback model redwood-llama-7b-quant (lower KV pressure). Command run: ```route set --org silvercrest --percent 30 --model redwood-llama-7b-quant --region us-west-2``` we'll see if tail improves.\n
alice_oncall: good. Monitoring p99 in real-time (Grafana).\n
incident-bot: Incident timeline: p99 spike start 08:12 UTC -> throttle 08:18 UTC -> route 30% to fallback 08:19 UTC -> observable p99 drop beginning 08:22 UTC.\n
emma_support: Luis, you should see fewer stalls now. Can you confirm customer-side behavior?\n
luis_silvercrest: yes, the stalls dropped a lot after 08:22. Still seeing some delayed sessions but much better. Thanks for the fast action.\n
carla_sre: collected traces show heavy K/V cache churn for prefixes longer than 1k tokens; eviction loops correlate with requests that use dynamic prompt concatenation. We need a permanent fix: either raise per-worker KV cache capacity for that pool, or recommend Silvercrest use prefix compression or canonicalization to reduce unique prefix keys.\n
ben_reliability: longer-term ops options: 1) enable sticky routing by client fingerprint so repeated prefixes reuse same hot worker; 2) increase KV cache retention for dedicated-pool-4; 3) improve backpressure to reject or queue sessions gracefully when KV pressure crosses threshold.\n
dave_engine: engineering note: there's a race in the KV cache refill path when many sessions try to populate KV simultaneously; causes lock contention leading to GC churn. I can push a mitigative hotfix to reduce lock granularity and add instrumentation. Will need a canary.\n
alice_oncall: prioritize: 1) formal post-incident triage, 2) customer follow-up + recommended usage pattern, 3) engineering hotfix + canary. For now, keep the throttle for 1 hour and keep 30% route to fallback until we confirm stability.\n
emma_support: I'll draft a support note for Silvercrest explaining recommended mitigations: concurrency limits, prefix canonicalization, and guidance on streaming vs batch for demos. Luis, we'll sync on the wording.\n
luis_silvercrest: appreciated. Also can you whitelist a small set of IPs that need full throughput for real-time demo presenters? We can limit demo traffic to those and keep rest throttled.\n
carla_sre: we can create an exception with an allowlist for up to 6 client IPs: ```./opsctl add-org-allowlist --org silvercrest --ips 3.12.45.6,3.12.45.7 --ttl 2h``` will need compliance sign-off but doable.\n
ben_reliability: next steps for engineering: Dave will open PR for KV lock reduction and extra metrics (KV eviction rate, per-prefix resident set). We'll schedule canary to a non-prod dedicated pool, then roll to us-west-2.\n
dave_engine: opening PR now, linking to this thread: https://git.internal/r/kv-lock-reduce. I'll coordinate canary with Carla for a maintenance window.\n
alice_oncall: summary for postmortem: root cause = KV cache thrash triggered by sudden high-concurrency long-prefix workload from single-tenant; contributing = lack of org-level concurrency caps + KV lock contention. Mitigations performed = org throttle, partial routing to quantized fallback, pprof/traces collected, allowedlist for demo IPs. Action items: support guide for customers, engineering hotfix + canary, improve autoscaling and graceful backpressure.\n
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident owner: alice_oncall. Severity: Sev3 (customer impact but mitigated).\n
alice_oncall: I'll run the postmortem template and set owners. Closing this thread once canary passes and Silvercrest signs off. Thanks team :thumbsup:\n
emma_support: ping @luis_silvercrest to schedule a 30-min follow-up tomorrow to review best practices.\n
luis_silvercrest: yes please, morning PST works. Thanks again everyone.\n
carla_sre: attaching uploaded pprof and traces: gs://redwood-pprof/silvercrest/4951234567/snapshot1.pprof (link), traces in jaeger under trace id 0b2f4a.\n
ben_reliability: I'll keep monitoring the metrics for the next 2 hours. If p99 reappears, revert routing and escalate to Sev2.\n
alice_oncall: acknowledged. Thread will be archived into incidents once all action items are created.
